title: Incidence mapping-space bridge for the relative Segal test
statement:
Use coherent functor quasicategories, mapping spaces and homotopy limits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations as in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], and relative cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. For $r\geq0$, let $I_r$ have vertices $v_0,\ldots,v_r$, edges $a_1,\ldots,a_r$, and only nonidentity arrows $a_i\to v_{i-1},a_i\to v_i$. Put $K=N(I_r)$. For any quasicategory $X$, object $z$ and coherent diagram $f:K\to X$, there is a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)}(\Delta_Kz,f)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_{\alpha\in I_r}\operatorname{Map}_X(z,f(\alpha)).$$
Let $p:X\to B$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, where $B$ is the nerve of a small ordinary category. Given a cone $x\to f$, the square with upper row $\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)}(\Delta_Kz,f)$ and lower row its image in $B$ is a homotopy pullback if and only if, for every $\phi:pz\to px$, the induced comparison
$$\operatorname{Map}_X^\phi(z,x)\longrightarrow\operatorname{holim}_{\alpha\in I_r}\operatorname{Map}_X^{p(x\to f(\alpha))\phi}(z,f(\alpha))$$
is an equivalence. Superscripts denote homotopy fibers over the specified base arrows; these comparisons and equivalences are natural in the entire cone and in $p$.

source.place: Definition A.3.1(2), relative Segal cones; the mapping-space verification for the mapping cylinder. Online source; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Choose nested universes large enough for $X,B$ and their mapping spaces; $K=N(I_r)$ is small. Put $F(\alpha)=\operatorname{Map}_X(z,f(\alpha))$ and $1_K=\Delta_K*$ in $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S)$. The constant-source section comparison gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)}(\Delta_Kz,f)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(1_K,F)$. For any space-valued diagram $T:K\to\mathcal S$, the dual transport classification represents $T$ by a right fibration over $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ and represents $1_K$ by the identity right fibration. Its mapping-space formula identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(1_K,T)$ with the section space of this right fibration. The right-fibration section-limit theorem identifies that section space, with its evaluation cone, with $\operatorname{holim}_{K}T$. Apply this with $T=F$. Transport along each incidence arrow is postcomposition with its image under $f$, by the mapping-bifunctor clause of transport classification. Thus this is the required homotopy limit over $I_r$, with its specified projections.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.3.4 and Remark 3.3.3.5, combined with the existing constant-source comparison; agent specialization to the incidence diagram

proof.text: Write $\lambda:\Delta_Kx\to f$ for the given cone and put $U=\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x)$, $V=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,X)}(\Delta_Kz,f)$, $C=\operatorname{Map}_B(pz,px)$ and $D=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_Kpz,pf)$. The horizontal maps are composition with $\lambda$ and $p\lambda$. For $\phi\in C$, its image in $D$ is the transformation $\psi_\phi=(p\lambda)\circ\Delta_K\phi$, whose component is $\psi_{\phi,\alpha}=p(\lambda_\alpha)\phi$. It is not $\Delta_K\phi$: the target diagram $pf$ need not be constant. The cone and the functor $p$ specify the commutation homotopy of this square, retaining its higher composition data.

source.place: Definition A.3.1(2), relative limit condition; agent expansion of the induced mapping-space square

proof.text: Let $G(\alpha)=\operatorname{Map}_B(pz,pf(\alpha))$. Applying the section comparison in Step 1 to $X$ and $B$ identifies $V\to D$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(1_K,F)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(1_K,G)$ induced by $p$. The point $\psi_\phi$ corresponds to a coherent transformation $b_\phi:1_K\to G$. Form $H_\phi=F\times^h_G1_K$ using $b_\phi$. The pointwise-limit clause gives this pullback in $\mathcal C$ and identifies its value at $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{hofib}_{\psi_{\phi,\alpha}}(F(\alpha)\to G(\alpha))$. The representable $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(1_K,-)$ preserves this pullback. Since $1_K$ is terminal by the same pointwise-limit clause, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(1_K,1_K)$ is contractible. Consequently the resulting pullback is exactly $\operatorname{hofib}_{\psi_\phi}(V\to D)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(1_K,H_\phi)$. Step 1 identifies the latter with $\operatorname{holim}_\alpha H_\phi(\alpha)$. This gives the asserted homotopy limit of relative mapping spaces with the varying base arrows and their coherent incidence maps.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.2.2 and Corollary 5.1.2.3, pointwise limits; Proposition 5.1.3.2, representables preserve limits; agent application to a pullback along b_phi

proof.text: Take the path pullback $P=V\times^h_D C$ and its comparison $e:U\to P$ supplied by the square's commutation homotopy. The mapping-path replacement of $V\to D$ is a Kan fibration over $D$; hence $P\to C$, its pullback, is a Kan fibration (a horn lifting problem pulls back to the same horn lifting problem upstairs). Its strict fibre at $\phi$ is, degree by degree, $V\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\{\psi_\phi\}$, which is $\operatorname{hofib}_{\psi_\phi}(V\to D)$. The strict-to-path-pullback comparison identifies this strict fibre with $\operatorname{hofib}_{\phi}(P\to C)$. Apply the existing homotopy-fibre detection theorem to $e$ over $\mathrm{id}_C$. It says $e$ is an equivalence exactly when every map $\operatorname{hofib}_\phi(U\to C)\to\operatorname{hofib}_{\psi_\phi}(V\to D)$ is an equivalence. The definition of homotopy pullback identifies the first condition with the required square test. The first fibre is $\operatorname{Map}_X^\phi(z,x)$ by definition, and Step 3 identifies the second with the displayed homotopy limit. These identifications prove both implications.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.7.1 in the existing homotopy-fibre formulation; path replacement 0101 and strict/path comparison 0329; agent application to e over id_C

proof.text: The map on fibres just obtained is the stated comparison, not an unspecified equivalence: the constant-source comparison sends postcomposition by $\lambda$ to the family $u\mapsto\lambda_\alpha u$. After applying $p$, its base component is $p(\lambda_\alpha)\phi=\psi_{\phi,\alpha}$. Pullback projections therefore give precisely the maps into each $H_\phi(\alpha)$, with their incidence homotopies. The section/limit theorem preserves these evaluation maps, and representable preservation of pullbacks is natural in the entire span. Restriction, application of a functor to arrow simplices, and composition of the specified path homotopies commute with maps of cones and with commutative maps of $p:X\to B$. Thus the equivalences and comparisons are natural in all the stated data. For $r=0$ the section limit is a one-object limit; if $C$ is empty then $U=P=\varnothing$ and the fibre test is vacuous, as required. Empty individual mapping spaces and fibres are allowed throughout.
